table.header: PA similarity network construction and seed selection

table.text: Overview of LocPA. (a) LocPA takes individual 24-hour physical activity (PA) profiles as input. (b) A generalized additive model (GAM) adjusts PA profiles for age, sex and body mass index (BMI) to obtain PA residual profiles. (c) A PA similarity network is constructed from the residual profiles, and representative seed participants are selected to cover the entire cohort while reducing the number of statistical tests. (d) Local enrichment tests assess disease prevalence or future incidence risk within each seed neighborhood, followed by weighted Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment for multiple testing. (e) Disease-enriched seeds are grouped using Louvain community detection algorithm. (f) The resulting disease-enriched groups are characterized by disease prevalence or incidence risk and associated clinical markers.

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Between 2013 and 2015, approximately 100,000 participants participated in the UKB accelerometry substudy, wearing wrist-worn triaxial accelerometers that continuously recorded physical activity for up to seven days 5, 19.

> Participants were excluded if their accelerometer recordings were of poor quality, had insufficient wear time or could not be adequately calibrated.

> All UKB participants provided written informed consent, and the UK Biobank study received ethical approval from the relevant institutional review boards.

> Participants were classified as having a disease if they reported having been told by a healthcare professional that they had the corresponding condition.

> This procedure was repeated until all participants were covered by at least one selected neighborhood.

> Overview of LocPA. (a) LocPA takes individual 24-hour physical activity (PA) profiles as input. (b) A generalized additive model (GAM) adjusts PA profiles for age, sex and body mass index (BMI) to obtain PA residual profiles. (c) A PA similarity network is constructed from the residual profiles, and representative seed participants are selected to cover the entire cohort while reducing the number of statistical tests. (d) Local enrichment tests assess disease prevalence or future incidence risk within each seed neighborhood, followed by weighted Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment for multiple testing. (e) Disease-enriched seeds are grouped using Louvain community detection algorithm. (f) The resulting disease-enriched groups are characterized by disease prevalence or incidence risk and associated clinical markers.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
